title: Rumble in the Bronx
tagline: New York welcome. Hong Kong kicks.
about: A Hong Kong cop visiting his uncle in New York ends up protecting a supermarket from a street gang.

    StartersElaine's supermarket Reuben bitesToasted rye topped with pastrami, sauerkraut and melted Swiss cheeseHow to make it6 slices of rye bread250g sliced pastrami150g sauerkraut, drained150g Swiss cheese4 tbsp mayonnaise1 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp horseradish1 dill pickle, chopped4 slices of dill pickle, to garnishCut the rye into quarters and toast lightly at 200°C.Top each with folded pastrami, sauerkraut and a square of Swiss cheese.Bake until melted.Mix the mayonnaise with tomato sauce, horseradish and chopped pickle.Dab on each bite and spear with a slice of dill pickle.Pork and chive dumplingsPan-fried pork and garlic chive dumplings with black vinegarHow to make it400g pork mince1 bunch garlic chives, chopped1 tbsp grated ginger1 tsp sesame oil30 dumpling wrappers2 tbsp Chinkiang vinegar1 tbsp oilMix the pork with chives, ginger and sesame oil.Fill the wrappers and pleat.Fry until crisp underneath.Add water and steam under a lid.Serve with black vinegar.Danny's chicken and shiitake baoFor Danny, Nancy's little brother, who keeps an eye on the storeHow to make it400g chicken mince6 dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked and chopped3 spring onions, sliced10g ginger, grated2 tbsp oyster sauce1 tbsp soy sauce1 tsp sesame oil12 frozen plain bao bunsMix the chicken, shiitake, spring onion, ginger, oyster sauce, soy and sesame oil.Stir-fry the filling until cooked and sticky.Open the bao and spoon in the filling.Steam until hot through.Jamaican beef pattiesTony's gang trashed aisle three. Grab one anyway.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsHovercraft sweet and sour porkCrispy pork tossed in pineapple and pepper sweet and sour sauceHow to make it700g pork shoulder, diced1 egg100g cornflour2 L vegetable oil, for frying1/2 pineapple1 red capsicum80ml white vinegar80g caster sugar80ml tomato sauce300g jasmine riceCut the pineapple and capsicum into chunks and toss the pork in egg and cornflour.Cook the rice.Fry the pork in batches in the oil at 180°C until crisp.Simmer the pineapple and capsicum with vinegar, sugar and tomato sauce, then thicken.Toss the pork through and serve with the rice.Ginger and spring onion lobster noodlesHis uncle's wedding banquetHow to make itAs written, serves 4Lobster tails cut through the shell and wok-fried with ginger and spring onion in a light oyster sauce, piled over crisp-edged soft egg noodles.Cut 4 lobster tails through the shell into chunks, or use 800g king prawns.Dust in cornflour and fry in a hot wok for 2 minutes, then set aside.Pan-fry 400g boiled egg noodles in oil until crisp underneath.Stir-fry 50g sliced ginger and 6 spring onion lengths, add the lobster, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine and 150ml chicken stock and toss 2 minutes.Pour over the noodles.SweetsAlmond jelly with fruitChilled almond milk jelly cubes with lychees and mandarin segmentsHow to make it4 gelatine leaves500ml full cream milk60g caster sugar1 tsp almond extract425g tin lychees2 mandarinsSoak the gelatine leaves in cold water.Warm the milk with the sugar, then stir in the gelatine and almond extract.Set in a tray for 3 hours.Cut into cubes.Serve in bowls with lychees and mandarin segments in their syrup.DrinksUncle Bill's wedding iced jasmine teaIced jasmine tea with lychee syrup, lime and lychees in the glassHow to make it1 L water5 tsp jasmine tea565g tin lychees1 lime1 bag iceHeat the water to just off the boil and steep the jasmine tea.Strain and cool, and drain the lychees keeping the syrup.Stir some of the lychee syrup and lime juice into the tea.Chill for an hour.Fill four tall glasses with ice and a few lychees, pour in the tea and finish with a twist of lime
